post.title: S&P 500 closed 8.2% off its record. What's a correction?
post.ig:
The S&P 500 fell 2% Thursday to 7,175.83, its sixth straight loss and 8.2% below its Oct. 6 record close (AP).
The Dow dropped 1,101 points, or 2.2%, and more than 90% of S&P 500 stocks fell (AP).
Reports blamed doubts that heavy AI spending will pay off.
A correction means 10% off the high. For the S&P 500 that line is about 7,037 (our math).
By one Motley Fool count, 10% drops have come about once every 1.85 years since 1950, on average.
Figures as of Thursday's close. Sources: AP, Motley Fool.
